text:
eva: heads up — ran into a weird repro with the JS SDK in an edge sample app using Vite. auth retries + ESM/CJS interop seem to trigger duplicate token refreshes and 401 loops when running on the edge runtime. anyone seen this? :thinking:

matt: ugh. do you have a minimal repro? which bundler + build target?

eva: simple repro: Vite (4.x), target="es2022", SSR function deployed to Vercel Edge / Cloudflare Workers. SDK installed from npm (stable). Steps: clone https://github.com/redwood/repro-edge-auth (private demo), npm i, npm run build, npm run dev (vercel). Hitting /api/generate causes 401 -> SDK calls refresh -> second call sends old token again -> infinite-ish retries.

jen: does the request actually include the refreshed token on subsequent attempts?

eva: nope — logs show the refresh handler runs and returns new token, but the following outgoing request still has the old Authorization header. looks like the header mutation isn't applied when the module gets transformed by the bundler.

sam: that smells like a bundler default-import/export transform. if the SDK does something like `module.exports = { default: Client }` and the bundler rewrites imports, you can end up with `client.default` vs `client` confusion. in ESM-first runtimes that can cause ambiguous references — but usually it's just a runtime crash, not auth retention.

matt: another vector: edge runtimes replace global `fetch` and sometimes our auth middleware relies on a small side-effect import to patch Request/Headers semantics. tree-shaking or CJS->ESM conversion can drop that side-effect. did you notice any `ReferenceError: Headers is not a constructor`?

eva: no header error. i added debug logs inside the SDK where we set auth header in the request interceptor. they show header mutated on the request object we create, but by the time the edge runtime sends it, header reverted. i'll paste the minimal interceptor: 

```js
// inside sdk/lib/request.js
export async function send(req) {
  if (needsRefresh()) {
    const newToken = await auth.refresh(); // returns token string
    req.headers.set('authorization', `Bearer ${newToken}`);
  }
  return fetch(req);
}
```

matt: looks fine. can you show the built output for that file (post-bundle)? sometimes esbuild rewrites `req.headers.set` to `headers_set(req.headers, ...)` and if a polyfill replaced Headers with immutable map it won't mutate. also check `commonjs` plugin transforms.

sam: repro tip: in Vite config try `build.commonjsOptions.transformMixedEsModules = true` and `esbuild: { target: 'es2019' }` — we've seen that fix import shape for some CJS packages.

eva: i tried changing esbuild target to es2019 and it actually made the behavior go away locally. but can't require customers to downgrade target. i want to capture a small repro for the SDK team and a suggested fix.

jen: does this reproduce with Rollup or Webpack?

eva: quick test: Rollup (node) + @rollup/plugin-commonjs also reproduces the stale-header behaviour when bundling the SDK as CJS -> ESM interop. webpack (test) didn't reproduce on my machine, but our internal CI uses webpack 5 with module federation — could be flaky.

sam: two potential fixes on SDK side: 1) ensure the auth middleware uses immutable pattern that returns a new Request object with updated headers instead of mutating in-place, e.g.:

```js
const updated = new Request(req, { headers: { ...Object.fromEntries(req.headers), authorization: `Bearer ${newToken}` } });
return fetch(updated);
```

that avoids relying on real `Headers` mutability. 2) ship both ESM and CJS entry points with faithful default and named exports so bundlers don't mangle default export shape.

matt: +1 to 1). it's less fiddly for runtimes. also add a test that simulates a fetch polyfill that returns frozen Headers.

eva: i can prototype the immutable approach in the repro. also discovered another twist: when Vite builds with `ssr: { noExternal: ['@redwood/sdk'] }` it bundles a different shape and the bug disappears. so it's definitely a bundler transform issue.

sam: can you paste your vite.config.js?

eva: sure: 

```js
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
export default defineConfig({
  build: {
    ssr: true,
    target: 'es2022',
    rollupOptions: { external: ['@redwood/sdk'] }
  }
})
```

sam: try removing `external` or set `build.commonjsOptions.include: [/node_modules/]`. sometimes leaving the SDK external causes runtime to load the package variant that relies on node-only shims.

jen: also add a test for the SDK around `fetch` retry flow in an environment that freezes Headers; we should catch this early.

eva: created a minimal patch to use new Request + merged headers and the repro stops reproducing even with current Vite target. pushed branch `fix/immutable-auth-headers` to the repro repo. would you like the link?

matt: please open a PR against SDK repo with the patch + unit test + a tiny Vite repro in samples. mark it as release candidate for patch-level fix. include note in changelog about ESM/CJS packaging shape.

sam: i'll also look into packaging: ensure package.json has `exports` map for both `.` and `./cjs` and add an `import` and `require` entrypoint that are consistent. and add a short note in the developer docs about Vite/SSR caveats (commonjsOptions).

eva: awesome — thanks all. i'll PR the repro and patch. cc @deploy-bot :rocket:

deploy-bot: noted. created ticket INF-1278 and assigned to sam/matt for SDK packaging + tests. ETA: next minor.

matt: nice find eva — this one could've bitten customers. once the PR lands can we backport to the current stable major?

sam: yes, likely a patch. i'll triage after review.

eva: follow-up: added a short runbook to the repro README with these quick mitigations: 1) set esbuild target <= es2019 2) set build.commonjsOptions.transformMixedEsModules=true 3) noExternal the SDK so Vite bundles it consistently 4) upgrade to patched SDK.

matt: perfect. thanks for the detailed repro + steps. :clap:
